correctness.rationale: For n=2^k p q, M=2^(k+1)-1, x=p-M>0 even, abundance a=M(p+1)-xq and a<Mp<pq. Distinct proper divisors below a reduce semiperfectness to a=r+sp+tq (0<=r,s,t<=M). When weird and a>=q, both terminal residues t=0 and t=1 exceed M; their differences give nonzero delta with |delta|<=x-2, then a≡-x(delta+1) mod p. Since (x-1)^2<=M forces p>x(x-1), no possible positive, -1, or <=-2 delta can yield an admissible forbidden short residue. Thus a<q; the t=0 residue alone yields precisely M(p+1)/(x+1)<q<Mp/x and 1<=[x(q+1)]_p<=x-1. The converse is exact. The derived abundance bound is strict. Fresh independent proper-divisor coefficient enumeration agreed for 6,867 positive-abundance prime pairs through k=7, including 2^3*19*61 with a=56; finite tests do not prove all k.

evidence: General three-quarter bound a<3M²/4+M is larger than (M+1)(M+2)/3 for sufficiently large M.
Iannucci conjectures, rather than proves, the stronger universal abundance bound.
broader_coverage.reasoning: A broader family with weaker parameter bounds does not dominate the new conditional sharper theorem; the published general subset criterion does not automatically simplify in this strip.

originality.rationale: Iannucci 2015 already developed the general semiperfectness subset-sum obstruction and a finite k<=14 census, and conjectured the one-third-scale abundance bound. A published all-prime three-quarter bound is weaker; it does not imply the conjectured bound in this square-root strip or the exact one-residue iff criterion. A genuinely new short-gap two-residue exclusion is required. Unknown historically equivalent formulations remain possible.
